title: EMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates Compromised
description: Eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys belonging to Indian CA eMudhra Limited were compromised due to insufficient randomness in the certificate generation process. This cryptographic weakness allows attackers to derive private keys from public certificates, enabling unauthorized TLS certificate signing and potential man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks. Major browser and OS vendors have revoked trust in these intermediates, and eMudhra has revoked the eight compromised certificates. Organizations are advised to audit PKI assets, reissue certificates from trusted CAs, enforce strict revocation checking, and update trust stores to mitigate risk. Palo Alto Networks provides solutions and guidance to assist with managing this incident and preventing exploitation.
aiSummary: The eMudhra incident involves the compromise of eight intermediate CA private keys caused by a critical cryptographic defect—specifically, insufficient randomness during key generation. This flaw allows attackers to derive private keys from the corresponding public certificates, enabling them to sign unauthorized TLS certificates and perform MitM interception, impersonation, or session hijacking against targeted domains. The compromised intermediates have been revoked by eMudhra and untrusted by major browsers and operating systems. Palo Alto Networks recommends comprehensive discovery and auditing of PKI assets, immediate certificate reissuance from alternative trusted CAs, emergency trust store updates to distrust affected intermediates, strict enforcement of certificate revocation checking, and active threat hunting for signs of misuse. Long-term mitigations include implementing Certificate Transparency monitoring, enforcing Certificate Authority Authorization DNS records, and hardening automated certificate lifecycle management. Palo Alto Networks also offers products and services to assist customers in managing and responding to this compromise.
aiImpact: The compromise of eMudhra intermediate CA private keys allows attackers to derive private keys from public certificates, enabling unauthorized signing of TLS certificates. This can lead to man-in-the-middle interception, impersonation, and session hijacking against domains relying on these certificates. The incident undermines trust in TLS communications secured by the affected intermediates, potentially exposing organizations and users to interception and impersonation attacks. Major browsers and OS vendors have revoked trust in these intermediates, and eMudhra has revoked the compromised certificates to mitigate further risk.
